title: English Composition for Multilingual Students I
description: Introduction to college-level writing for language/grammar needs of first-semester English learners. Understanding written argument, comprehension of college-level academic texts, and integrating ideas and information from multiple text sources in formal written papers.
notes: Not open to native speakers of English.

title: English Composition for Multilingual Students II
description: College-level writing; attention to language needs of advanced English learners. Written argument, comprehension and analysis of college-level academic texts, and use of multiple text sources for written synthesis and argument.
notes: Not open to native speakers of English. Not open to students with credit in a higher-numbered composition course or AFRAS 120 or AMIND 120 or CCS 111B or RWS 100 [or ECL 100] or RWS 105B.

title: Introduction to Language
description: The nature of language. Sound, meaning, and grammar. Language history and change. Dialects and variation. Language acquisition. Animal communication. Language and the brain.
notes: Not open to students with credit in upper division linguistics courses, excluding

title: Machines, Minds, and Society
description: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning from the perspectives of history, culture, and the social sciences. Technological advances in “thinking machines” in social and political contexts. Applications in work, media, education, and health. Social and ethical implications.

title: Advanced Composition for Multilingual Students
description: Satisfaction of the SDSU Written Communication Assessment requirement; and completion of LING 100B with a grade of C- or better.
notes: Not open to students with credit in AFRAS 200, AMIND 225, CCS 200, or RWS 200 [or ECL 200].

title: Elementary Statistics for Language Studies
description: Introductory statistics and probability using language data to illustrate statistical ideas and facilitate analyses of quantitative language data. Measures of central tendency and dispersion, correlation, mixed models, regression, and significance. Probabilistic explanation in linguistics.

title: Experimental Topics
description: Selected topics.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.

title: Academic and Professional Writing for Multilingual Students
description: Advanced expository writing, with practice in the various associated skills (organization, research, presentation, rhetoric). The goal is to enable non-native English speakers to function completely with written English on advanced university levels. This course may not be used toward the major or minor in linguistics.

title: Body Talk: Language, Bodily Behavior, and Social Interaction
description: Study of how language, gesture, and embodied behavior shape real-time interaction. Examines how speech and bodily conduct work together to perform social actions and manage social relationships. Cross-cultural miscommunication.

title: How to Spot a Liar
description: Analyze the role of language in lying across domains and communities. Apply tools from pragmatics and related areas to examine how word choice, pronunciation, and grammar change in untrue statements at the interpersonal and societal levels.

title: Language and Politics
description: Linguistics devices used to persuade in politics. Differences between what is literally said and what is actually conveyed in political discourse. How political speakers and writers use grammar, sound structure, and vocabulary to persuade.

title: Why Do We Talk Like That? Dialect variation in English
description: Regional accents and dialect diversity of English in the United States and elsewhere. Stereotypes about dialects, portrayal of dialects in pop culture, and how dialects change over time.

title: Language and Advertising
description: Linguistic devices used to persuade in advertising. Differences between what is literally said and what is actually conveyed in advertisements. How advertisers use the grammar, sound structure, and vocabulary of languages (especially English) to persuade audiences.

title: Language Across the Lifespan
description: The scientific study of language. Effect of normal and pathological aging on language knowledge and use. Language learning in cognitively impaired individuals. Native and second language acquisition and use in childhood and adulthood. Cognitive benefits of bilingualism.

title: Language and Computers
description: Computers, computer programming languages, and “artificial intelligence” viewed from perspective of human language.

title: Sociocultural Analysis of Black Languages
description: Social and cultural functions of Black languages, verbal and nonverbal, in Afro-American life, and their profound impact on larger society. Also, a probe into issues concerning validity of Black English.
notes: This course satisfies the ethnic studies [ES] requirement.

title: Linguistics and English
description: Introduction to sound and grammatical structure of language, with special attention to English. Language acquisition and variation. Of special interest to prospective teachers. Not open to students with credit in

title: English Grammar for Prospective Teachers
description: Core grammatical concepts and facts of English grammar. Parts of speech; grammatical relations; word, sentence, discourse structure. Focus on standard written English. Of special interest to prospective secondary school teachers.

title: Language Acquisition
description: Principles of child language development. Sounds and grammar in speech of young children. Acquisition of reading and vocabulary. Relationship between cognitive development and language. Development of language in bilinguals. Second language acquisition.

title: Heritage Language Acquisition
description: Linguistic properties of heritage languages, which are minority languages acquired in the home by bilinguals who become dominant in the main societal language. Cultural and social aspects of language use, language education, and issues of equity in heritage language research.

title: Second Language Acquisition
description: Basic facts about the acquisition of nonnative languages in adulthood to include beginning and end points, implicit and explicit learning, individual differences, input and output, ordered development, and the role of instruction.

title: Community-Based Language Fieldwork
description: Fieldwork in language use in community setting. Students observe, keep field notes, analyze language behavior (e.g. speaking, reading, writing, listening).

title: American Indian Languages
description: Structures of American Indian languages. Language families of North America, history, and present circumstances. Interdependence of language and culture, differences in ways of speaking. Issues of language endangerment, language death, language maintenance, and language revitalization.
notes: This course satisfies the ethnic studies [ES] requirement.

title: How We Meme, Emoji and Reel: Language in New Media
description: Exploration of how digital technologies shape language use through informal writing, multimodal communication, and online discourse. Covers Netspeak, memes, emojis, creativity, and AI, analyzing how language evolves in digital spaces with attention to theoretical frameworks, literacy, and critical debates.

title: Experimental Topics in Linguistics
description: Specialized study of a selected topic in linguistics.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.

title: Fundamentals of Linguistics
description: Principles of modern linguistics, with attention to English phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics and pragmatics; universals and typology.

title: Language in Mind and Society
description: Child language acquisition, adult language production/comprehension and sociolinguistics. Dialects, language variation, and standardization. Bilingualism and language change.

title: Functions of Language
description: Empirical methods in linguistics. Phonological structure of English and other languages. Functional and discourse related approaches to language patterns. Connections between morphosyntactic concepts and functional/discourse concepts to conduct text analysis.

title: Writing for Graduate Students
description: Conventions of scholarly writing appropriate for student papers, theses, or academic journal articles. Development of research questions and literature reviews as appropriate for students’ disciplines. Revision of current or previous course papers according to disciplinary conventions.

title: Phonology
description: Theoretical principles of transformational-generative phonology.

title: Syntax
description: Theoretical principles of transformational-generative syntax.

title: Morphology
description: Theoretical principles of words structure, including inflection, derivation, and compounding; organization of the lexicon; structure of inflectional paradigms; morphophonological and morphosyntactic alterations; and computational applications.

title: Semantics and Pragmatics
description: Advanced semantic theory; systematic analysis of the interaction of sequences of language with real world context in which they are used.

title: Discourse Analysis
description: Theories of discourse structure. Text and context. Frameworks for analyzing written and spoken discourses such as genre analysis, conversation analysis, critical discourse analysis, discourse and grammar, speech act theory, and corpus linguistics. Applications of discourse analysis such as cross-cultural misunderstanding.

title: English Grammar
description: English morphology, syntax, and discourse structure, including simple and complex sentence structure; lexical categories and subcategories; discourse functions of selected constructions. Problems and solutions in teaching English grammar.

title: Theory and Practice of English as a Second Language
description: The nature of language learning; evaluation of techniques and materials for the teaching of English as a second language.

title: Sociolinguistics
description: Investigation of the correlation of social structure and linguistic behavior.

title: Psycholinguistics
description: Psychological and mental processes related to comprehension, production, perception, and acquisition of language in adults and children.

title: Bilingualism
description: Bilingualism in society and in schools. Cognition, language processing, and representation in bilinguals. Research methods in the study of bilingualism.

title: Practical Issues in Teaching English as a Second Language
description: Practical approaches to applications of the theory of English as a Second Language (ESL) and methodology for speaking, reading, listening, writing; techniques for facilitating growth of communicative competence.

title: Computer Assisted Language Learning and Teaching
description: Theory and practice of computer assisted language learning and language teaching. Hands-on experience with pedagogical aspects of using technology in the language classroom.

title: Computational Corpus Linguistics
description: Practical introduction to computation with text corpora and introduction to Python. Tokenizing, part-of-speech tagging, and lemmatizing (stemming) large corpora. Writing of Python programs required.

title: Python Scripting for Social Science
description: Python scripting for social science data. Statements and expressions. Strings, lists, dictionaries, files. Python with unformatted data (regular expressions). Graphs and social networks. Spatial data and simple GIS scripts.

title: Computational Linguistics
description: Basic concepts in computational linguistics including finite-state transducers, n-gram language models, vector space semantics, statistical classifiers, neural nets, and transformers. Applications to parsing, natural language understanding, and large language models.

title: Statistical Methods in Text Analysis
description: Statistical methods for analysis of large texts to include classification, clustering, vector space models, and the use of Large Language Models (LLMs). Data collection and annotation. Applications to include retrieval-augmented generation, relation detection, sentiment analysis, and topic modeling.

title: Selected Topics in Linguistics
description: Advanced study of selected topics.

title: Research Practicum
description: Participation in a specific research activity under faculty supervision. Maximum credit three units toward the major and minor in linguistics.

title: Professional Development in Linguistics
description: Introduction to the profession and to the skills and knowledge necessary for a professional in Linguistics and in English Language Teaching. Students engage in presentations by professionals and in a series of focused workshops.

title: Advanced Study of Language in Mind and Society
description: Language acquisition, psycholinguistics, and sociolinguistics. Mental and social influences on language learning and representation. Cognitive models of language production and processing. Rational speech acts and other social models of language comprehension.

title: Topics in Historical Linguistics
description: Methods and principles used in historical study of language; processes of language change in phonology, syntax, and semantics; linguistics reconstruction; origin of language; language families; development of writing. Analysis of Indo-European, Old English, or Middle English.

title: Advanced Formal Syntax
description: Advanced study of formal syntactic theory.

title: Advanced English Phonology
description: English phonetics, phonemics, and phonological rules. Phonological differences among American English dialects. Survey of contemporary approaches to phonology.

title: Immigrant Languages
description: Contrastive structure of selected languages representing significant immigrant populations in San Diego; emphasis on phonological, orthographic, morphological, lexical and syntactic features.

title: Pragmatics
description: Gricean and neo-Gricean approaches to pragmatics; relevance theory; reference; presupposition; speech acts; information structure.

title: Heritage Language Bilingualism
description: Representation, processing, and acquisition of heritage languages, which are minority languages acquired in the home by bilinguals who become dominant in the main societal language.

title: Materials Development in Applied Linguistics
description: Materials development and adaptation for teaching English as a second language and a language other than English.

title: Seminar in Sociolinguistic Research in the Speech Community
description: Methods to include the collection of sociolinguistic data through interviews. Analysis of those data to address questions pertaining to language variation and change.

title: Second Language Acquisition
description: Analyses of theories of second language acquisition; theoretical and empirical bases of current second language teaching methodologies.

title: ESL Reading and Writing
description: Application of discourse and reading theory to the teaching and testing of ESL reading and writing. Issues of coherence, process-product, genre studies.

title: Language and Cognition
description: Language production, comprehension, and acquisition, as these relate to human cognition.

title: English for Specific Purposes and Content-Based Instruction
description: Theory, practice, and history of these two related approaches to ESL/EFL.

title: Quantitative Research Methods in Language Studies
description: Research design and quantitative research methods for linguistic applications. Critical evaluation of published research studies; empirical research project.

title: Foundations of Language Assessment
description: Fundamental principles and goals of language assessment and language assessment research: characteristics of assessment methods; analyzing test tasks; designing test items; describing test scores; approaches to estimating reliability; validity and validation; authenticity and impact.

title: Advanced Topics in Linguistics
description: Advanced study in specific areas of linguistics.

title: Internship in English as a Second Language and Foreign Language Teaching
description: Internship in teaching English as a second language and English as a foreign language, offering work experience with practicing professionals.

title: Seminar in Linguistics
description: Research in linguistics, course content varying according to instructor.

title: Advanced Research Practicum
description: Participation in a specific research activity under faculty supervision. Maximum combined credit of three units of

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.

title: Thesis
description: Preparation of a project or thesis for the master’s degree.

title: Thesis Extension
description: Registration required in any semester or term following assignment of RP in Course 799A in which the student expects to use the facilities and resources of the university; also student must be registered in the course when the completed thesis is granted final approval.

title: Comprehensive Examination Extension
description: Registration required of students whose only requirement is completion of the comprehensive examination for the master’s degree. Registration in 799C limited to two semesters.
